_what: southleft/ds-contracts-poc, MEASURED. Until now this repository had read it and argued from it - SUBMISSION-VDS-008 rests on it - and never harvested it. There was no artefact in vendor/ at all, so every claim about it lived in prose and could not be checked.
_why_it_matters: It is the only other system in this programme attempting the same thing: one contract feeding both Figma and code. The submission asking whether the register stays canonical cites it as the subject, and a case file whose subject is described only in prose is one the bench cannot inspect.
_and_it_fixes_fragile_evidence: SUBMISSION-VDS-008 names /var/tmp/claude/refs/ds-contracts-poc as evidence - a clone in a DISPOSABLE directory that can vanish between filing and ruling. This artefact is the durable form: the numbers, committed, with the commit they were taken at.

the_finding.claim: EVERY ONE OF ITS 264 TOKEN VALUES IS A REFERENCE. NOT ONE IS A LITERAL.
the_finding.detail: Across 51 contracts every anatomy.root.tokens value has the form {color.action.{variant}.background} - a path into a token layer, sometimes with the variant interpolated. Zero hex, zero px, zero font names.
the_finding.why_it_matters: This is the property that makes the format compatible with VDS S-2(4), which admits a requirement and refuses a realisation, and it is now MEASURED rather than asserted. It is also the strongest thing in this file: they arrived independently at the rule this programme enforces, and their corpus obeys it without exception.

three_of_my_own_claims_corrected: I described "an anatomy part TREE whose leaves are token references". The tree is one node. All 51 contracts have exactly ONE part, named root, and none nests. The schema may permit depth; the shipped corpus has none.

I described "six extraction adapters". extract/adapters/ holds THREE (cem, css-module, react-tsx). Six was a count of route DIRECTORIES under extract/ - there are nine - which is a different thing, named wrongly.
I described "51 hand-authored conformance cases". The manifest has 53. The 51 is the CONTRACT count and I had carried it across.

contracts.status: all 51 are draft. Not one has advanced past it.

bindings._what: Every prop carries BOTH a Figma binding and a code binding. 113 of 113, both sides.
bindings._note: The schema declares VARIANT, BOOLEAN, TEXT, INSTANCE_SWAP and NONE. The corpus uses THREE: TEXT 63, VARIANT 40, BOOLEAN 10. INSTANCE_SWAP and NONE are declared and unused, worth knowing before treating the vocabulary as proven.

states._what: Declared states across the whole corpus, and they are sparse.
states._note: Six of 51 parts carry a states block at all. VDS fixes nine states by S-5(3) and requires the required/drawn/built triple; this corpus declares hover six times, focus-visible twice, disabled once. The two systems are not measuring the same thing here.

conformance._what: Cases whose expected disposition is declared BEFORE the extractor runs, banned from importing the engine own predicates. Their words: an instrument built that way cannot be surprised.
conformance._reading: 22 CARRIED, 18 UNSUPPORTED, 11 REFUSED, 2 LOWERED. More than half are expected NOT to carry, which is an unusually honest suite.

their_own_ceiling: docs/22-generality.md: no library in the repo is captured past 11.9%, and they say so - "Nobody has run a component set large enough to hit". Any claim that this is a working general extractor is wider than their own evidence.
_what_this_is_not: A code review. Nothing here judges the implementation; it reads the schema, the differ, the emitter refusals and the gates, and counts what the corpus uses.
A verdict on the fork. SUBMISSION-VDS-008 is with the bench; this is evidence for it.

Exhaustive even now. The dashboard, the 55 figma-sync scripts, the computed-style spike and 9137 lines of emitter BODY are still unread. What is read is the CONTRACT SURFACE: the schema, the four mechanisms above, and every number quoted.
_depth_note: FIRST PASS counted the corpus and said so: "9137 lines of emitter, the parity differ and the dashboard were not read, only measured by size". This pass reads them. The distinction that runs through everything below is SCHEMA CAPABILITY versus CORPUS USAGE - the format can express far more than the 51 shipped contracts use, and quoting the schema as if it were the evidence is how this repository gets over-described.

schema_vs_corpus._what: The contract schema models much more than the corpus exercises. Both numbers matter and only one is evidence.

rows.schema: a CLOSED union of 27 HTML elements (button, a, input, hr, kbd, fieldset ...)
rows.vds: VDS has NO equivalent. SUBMISSION-VDS-005 asks exactly this - where the primitive floor sits for the composition proof - and is pending. They answered it by ENUMERATION, which is a real answer and one the bench should see.

rows.schema: the ARIA role and the HTML element may each vary BY PROP, via a prop name and a value map
rows.vds: VDS has no way to say "this is a button when `as` is button and an anchor when it is link". A genuine capability gap, and the mechanism is small.

rows.schema: {prop, between:[a,b], aria: expanded|checked|pressed|selected} - a declarative toggle naming the ARIA attribute it drives
rows.vds: VDS records keyboard contract prose. This is the same fact made checkable, and it is the shape that would have caught Opbox's blocked-versus-disabled defect.

rows.schema: exactly three optional scalars: focusVisible (bool), minHitArea (number), contrast (AA|AAA)
rows.vds: VDS carries role, accessibleNameSource, keyboard[] and contrastFloors[] with basis and scope. CONFIRMED as filed in SUBMISSION-VDS-008: BREACH-0001 (a control boundary at 1.15:1 across five themes) is invisible to three scalars, because none of them names a PAIR of colours or a scope.

rows.schema: a part tree with slots, nested component instances and repeated collections (docs/16)
rows.corpus: ONE flat part named `root`, in all 51
rows.vds: the correction recorded in the first pass, now sharper: the tree exists in the SCHEMA and is unused in the CORPUS. My submission cited the tree as evidence; the schema supports the citation and the shipped work does not.

four_mechanisms_worth_taking.name: THE SYNC BOUNDARY, stated as a rule
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.what: docs/16: "The contract carries only canvas-expressible facts ... The contract will never carry hooks, event handlers, business logic, data fetching, side effects. Not not-yet - never, by design. Code is allowed to be arbitrarily richer than the canvas; the sync surface is capped at what a Figma component set can express, because that is the largest surface on which a DETERMINISTIC round trip is possible."
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.why: This is the clearest statement of the twin problem anyone in this programme has written, including me. It is also directly load-bearing on SUBMISSION-VDS-011: if the sync surface is capped at what a component set expresses, then a code module of variant exports is OUTSIDE the boundary by construction, and the question of what its coordinate is may dissolve rather than need deciding.
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.adopted: CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED BY STRUCTURE, [2026] VJS-CC-VIBE-DESIGN-SYSTEM 7 D4 - not adopted and no longer pending. The question it answers (which side is authoritative for a fact) is answered per-fact: the Figma file for what is DECIDED (OPBOX 3 D1), the register for what is CONTRACTED, the code for what is REALISED, and every crossing is a measured parity. A boundary that decides who overwrites whom presumes an overwrite path, and this system has none to govern.

four_mechanisms_worth_taking.name: FINDINGS CLASSIFIED ahead / behind / mismatch, per SURFACE
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.what: parity/diff.ts: every finding carries {surface: code|figma|figma-tokens, classification: ahead|behind|mismatch, subject, detail, remedy, proposedPatch?}. Always contract-versus-surface, never surface-to-surface.
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.why: VDS parity findings say expected and actual. They do not say WHICH SIDE MOVED. "The code is ahead of the contract" and "the code is behind it" are different jobs for different people, and one of them is usually an amendment rather than a fix. Cheap to adopt and it costs no design value.
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.adopted: ADOPTED 2026-07-31. `vds_core::Drift` (ahead/behind/mismatch/undetermined) on every Violation, set at the six parity emit sites that know the direction. Derivable here WITHOUT history, which is why it could be added at all: the direction follows from which side is MISSING the thing. R5 (the contract names a prop the code lacks) is BEHIND and an implementation is owed; R6 (the code accepts a prop no contract names) is AHEAD and an amendment is owed. `undetermined` is the default and prints nothing, because a line reading "drift: undetermined" on most findings would train a reader to skip the field on the ones that carry it. Proven on the real 13 findings from SUBMISSION-VDS-011: `direction: 13 behind`.

four_mechanisms_worth_taking.name: GOLDEN BYTES PER EMITTED FILE
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.what: evals/golden.json maps 265 emitted file paths to a sha256 each. Not a whole-run digest: a per-file one.
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.why: figma-draw is gated on two runs being byte-identical, which catches non-determinism and NOT an intended change slipping through unreviewed. A per-file golden turns every emitter change into a reviewable diff. This is strictly stronger than what this repository does.
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.adopted: site-factory/figma-golden.js (8c5e045). The golden is the LITERAL EMITTED BYTES in vendor/figma-draw.golden.js, not a per-file digest, which is where this departs from the source: a digest mismatch names no change, and the emitted script writes to the live Figma file, so the review surface has to be git diff. A drift is classified as data-moved (ordinary) or emitter-moved (needs eyes). The emitter's own digest is recorded and NOT judged on - listing it among the classified inputs, as the first version did, made the emitter_moved branch unreachable, and all four fabricated negative controls passed over that because they supply the digests they hand the classifier. Seeding a real edit into figma-draw.js is what caught it. DECISION-0006.

four_mechanisms_worth_taking.name: REFUSALS THAT NAME THE COMPOSITION RULE
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.what: emit-react.ts refuses by name: a part whose component ref creates a cycle ("a contract cannot compose itself"), structured values fixed in anatomy, and layoutByProp restyling a component instance ("the child contract owns its layout").
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.why: Each is a composition rule expressed as a refusal at emit time rather than as prose in a doc. VDS S-7(5) composition checks membership of may_use; it does not check for cycles, and nothing here would catch a block composing itself.
four_mechanisms_worth_taking.adopted: site-factory/block-graph.js (edc7853). A block that composes itself, directly or through another, is refused by name. CommonJS does not throw on a circular require - it hands back a half-built exports object - so nothing else would have said so.

parity_report._reading: total 0, and the acknowledgement baseline is an EMPTY array. So the differ, which is the most interesting instrument in the repository, has no findings to show. That is consistent with what they say themselves and it means the classification model above is a design worth taking and NOT a mechanism proven in use.

their_own_evidence_re_read.coverage_ceiling: no library captured past 11.9%, their own words, docs/22-generality.md
their_own_evidence_re_read._fairness: They state every one of these limits themselves, in committed docs, in numbers. That is rarer than the tooling and it is the reason this repository is worth reading at all.

adoption_tally._note: Three mechanisms in the tree with seeded failing directions each. The fourth was held for the court and the court dissolved the question rather than adopting the mechanism.
